changes: Share defensive exception conversion in an internal core helper; retain only integer failure statuses 400-599, otherwise 500.
Require a string Error message, retain fixed fallbacks for non-Error values and catch throwing property/prototype introspection.
Preserve explicit failure factories, query failure overloads, optional command data, null query sentinel and falsy success values.
Default unspecified IQueryHandler results to unknown rather than any; positive explicit result types, void commands and readonly metadata are compile-checked.
Remove redundant barrel stars without changing public class identities; the conversion helper is not added to the public barrel.
coverage_scope: Only command-result.ts, query-result.ts and result-error.ts: 27 executable lines, 20 branches; 100% line/statement/function/branch coverage. Interfaces/barrels use compiler and export-identity checks. No whole-backend coverage claim.
caller_scope: Static scan found fromError only at the two core method definitions, not production application callers. The three pre-fix HTTP failures are synthetic Fastify/ResponseHelper reproductions, not a demonstrated live endpoint vulnerability. Manual failure(error.message) call sites remain owning-module work.
dependency_reads: Complete ResponseHelper and HTTP error serializer read; representative login/get-profile handler paths inspected. No whole user/auth/business-module review implied.
limits: Results retain actual Error messages internally for diagnostics; HTTP responders must apply server-error redaction. This does not certify direct serialization of result objects or every application catch path.
Explicit failure() without status still defaults to client validation behavior at the HTTP boundary; it was not globally changed to 500.
Field-level domain serialization, nominal ID types, event composition and remaining shared-foundation reviews retain their open findings.
No persistence, schema or provider behavior changed. Database/provider checks were not rerun; prior 47-group database baseline remains historical.
